papers.title: Coal Exchange chit
lines: A million pounds' worth of coal sold in a morning, on a handshake.
The first one-million-pound cheque, the legend says, was written in this very room. Nobody has found the carbon copy.

papers.title: Letter from a Bevin Boy, 1947
lines: Dear Mam, they have sent me down the pit instead of into the Army. I asked for the Navy.
The foreman says the coal does not care where I wanted to go. He is right, but I still think it is unfair.
Send socks. Send bara brith. Send a cheerful letter that does not mention Dad's temper.

papers.title: Chapel minute book
lines: Minuted: the roof leaks over the harmonium. The harmonium has been moved. The leak has followed it.
Resolved: to pray for fair weather and to buy a bucket, in that order.

trail.clue: The chapel treasurer buried the building fund near the hedge during a flood in 1927. He died before he could say where, apparently.

papers.title: Match programme
lines: Wales v The Rest. The Rest are not expected to win. They have not been asked their opinion.
Hymns will be sung before the kick-off, during it, and afterwards, regardless of the result.

papers.title: Welsh rarebit scrap
lines: Toast, cheese, ale, mustard. Do not call it rabbit, whatever the English say.
Under it, in smaller type: 'The leek is the national emblem. It is also the national garnish.'

papers.title: Postcard from the sea
lines: Took the train from the valleys to the sea. First time. My daughter said 'it goes on forever'.
I said yes. She said, 'can we keep it?' I did not have an answer.
